concepts.why: The presence of a hypodense lesion in the middle ear, a fistula originating from the middle ear, and a hyperintense lesion at the edge of the petrous bone, along with a 2-centimeter mass found during drilling of the hypoplastic petrous bone, are consistent with a cholesteatoma.

The presence of discharge through the artificial ear canal and a fistula originating from the middle ear, along with a millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle, are consistent with a first branchial cleft anomaly.
The history of deep unilateral neck cellulitis, collection in the right parapharyngeal space and neck collection, and recurrence of neck cellulitis are consistent with temporal bone osteomyelitis.
The patient's history of unilateral otomandibular syndrome associated with severe temporal bone hypoplasia and recurrent neck cellulitis may be explained by a branchial cleft cyst.
